title: Screw Jack

introduction.definition: A screw jack (worm-gear screw jack) lifts or positions loads. A worm on the input shaft drives a worm wheel (gear) inside the housing; the worm wheel turns a nut or the screw, so the lifting screw moves up or down. The large gear ratio gives a high force from a small motor, and trapezoidal-thread jacks are usually self-locking, holding the load without a brake.
key_points: Trapezoidal screws usually self-locking; ball screws are not (need a brake)
Several jacks can be linked by shafts for synchronised lifting
introduction.summary: A screw jack lifts loads precisely. A motor turns the worm, which turns a bronze worm wheel; the wheel acts as a nut on the lifting screw, so the screw moves up or down. The high reduction makes it self-locking in many designs, holding the load without a brake.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Input torque = (load × lead) / (2π × η_screw × gear ratio × η_gear) — efficiency of trapezoidal jacks is low (often ~ 20–40 %), which is why they self-lock.

alignment: Align the jack so the screw is not side-loaded (use guides for the load); align connecting shafts in multi-jack systems.

commissioning: Function-test all motions and limit switches (hoist upper/lower, travel); check brakes; proof load test and thorough examination by a competent person before first use, per the applicable standard and local regulations.

routine.task: Listen for noise; check for backlash and screw lubrication.

periodic.task: Check backlash in worm gear and nut.

overhaul.task: Replace worm wheel/nut and bearings when backlash exceeds limits.

lubrication: Grease the screw and gearbox to schedule (high-pressure grease).

remedies: Reduce duty; larger jack; ball screw

safety: Never rely on self-locking under vibration — fit brakes/mechanical stops where people are underneath.

video_tutorials.title: Screw Jack — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Screw Jack.
A screw jack (worm-gear screw jack) lifts or positions loads.
A worm on the input shaft drives a worm wheel (gear) inside the housing; the worm wheel turns a nut or the screw, so the lifting screw moves up or down.
The large gear ratio gives a high force from a small motor, and trapezoidal-thread jacks are usually self-locking, holding the load without a brake.
Typical applications include lifting platforms and stages; positioning rolls, gates and antennas; synchronised multi-jack lifting systems; valve and damper actuation.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Gear Housing, Worm (input shaft), Worm Wheel (bronze) with Internal Thread (nut), Lifting Screw (Acme/trapezoidal) & Load Plate — translates.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Screw Jack.
Listen for noise; check for backlash and screw lubrication.
Check backlash in worm gear and nut.
Replace worm wheel/nut and bearings when backlash exceeds limits.
Watch for excessive backlash: load drops slightly on reversal. Common cause: worn nut/worm wheel.
Watch for overheating: hot housing, grease breakdown. Common cause: duty cycle exceeded.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
